URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/17/ukraine-cuts-off-crimea-from-russia-plunging-it-into-an-energy-crisis
(Full article via WebFetch — Al Jazeera newsroom)
Ukraine struck 147 tankers during the first 10 days of Operation Molochka (through July 16), 117 of them feeder tankers in the Sea of Azov and the remainder in the Black Sea.
Robert "Madyar" Brovdi (commander of Ukraine's unmanned forces): "paralyzes the feeder fleet of Russian courier tankers"; "It essentially prevents the export of 'black gold'"; "movement through the strait has been stopped"; "A deep and total blackout is inevitable."
Crimea occupation governor Sergey Aksyonov: "We cannot guarantee daily sales of gasoline at gas stations, nor can we provide precise schedules for fuel distribution." "There will be no precise schedules for electricity delivery."
Russian Deputy PM Alexander Novak admitted petrol shortages resulted because "our oil refineries are partially out of service due to incursions."
Russian FM Sergey Lavrov: the operation was "pure terrorism" — "What the Ukrainian regime is doing isn't even piracy any more."
Operation began July 6, 2026. (Cross-ref ISW/understandingwar: overnight July 20 Moscow-oblast oil depot + logistics + six Black Sea vessels struck; Zelensky reported four oil depots in Stavropol Krai July 19.)
